newsitem.title: JAPAN: Declining trend in Japan trade surplus slowing-MOF.
newsitem.headline: Declining trend in Japan trade surplus slowing-MOF.

text.p: The declining trend in Japan's trade surplus is slowing, a Ministry of Finance (MOF) official said on Thursday.
The official said although the rate of increase in imports continued to be greater than that of exports, in the last few months exports had shown year-on-year growth of more than 10 percent.
"The declining trend of Japan's trade surplus is slowing down," the official told a news conference.

The ministry earlier announced that Japan's customs-cleared trade surplus slid 26.8 percent in March from a year earlier to 818.34 billion yen. It also said the surplus for the business year which ended on March 31 declined 29.6 percent from a year earlier to 6.42 trillion yen.

Asked whether the weakening of the yen had led to a rise in exports, the official said: "It is difficult to make a clear judgment on the effects of exchange rates, but in general, a weak yen is one factor (behind the increase in exports)."
The official also said he could not predict the outlook regarding Japan's surplus with the United States.

He said exports to the United States, centring on cars and computers, were increasing, but that the trade account with the U.S. would be affected by various factors such as exchange rates and the economic conditions of the two countries.

The trade surplus with the U.S. rose 11.2 percent in March from a year earlier to 379.83 billion yen, while the surplus for the business year which ended in March showed a decline of 2.2 percent to 3.76 trillion yen. -- Tokyo Policy Desk (81-3-5473-3710)
